executable_mappings_summary.note: 47 executable requirements mapped from 10 external standards. 22 already implemented by prior rounds. 25 TODO items become the V2.2 and bench-upgrade backlog. This is the machine LEARNING from external standards, not just citing them.

what_makes_this_different_from_reference.old_approach: Add papers to a references folder. Cite them in the TTP. Hope the buyer reads them.
what_makes_this_different_from_reference.new_approach: Each standard becomes REQUIREMENTS → MACHINE ACTIONS → EVIDENCE RECORDS. The machine automatically generates verification steps, tracks completion, and produces buyer-grade evidence. The buyer doesn't need to read the standard — they see the machine has already executed it.
what_makes_this_different_from_reference.example: FDA says 'measure settling time.' The machine adds settling_time to the simulator and bench protocol, computes it for every run, and includes it in the evidence ledger. The buyer sees the metric, not the guidance document.

how_buyer_feedback_becomes_machine_actio.machine_action: BUYER_FEEDBACK_INTAKE_SCHEMA → category DESIGN_SUGGESTION → creates new attack mode 'posture_change' → runs in simulator → if V2.1 fails, creates V2.2 design requirement → re-verifies → updates TTP
how_buyer_feedback_becomes_machine_actio.this_is_the_loop: Buyer objection → new test case → new evidence → package update → re-evaluation. The buyer becomes a sensor in the invention engine.
